chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

In the case of a man to whom another man gave wealth to distribute among the poor, and he himself has dependents who are in need, should he give them from it without consulting the owner? He said, 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: Can a trustee use charity funds for his own family if he is in need?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility of *sadaqah* distribution, ruling that a trustee may prioritize his own needy dependents over the general poor without requiring the donor's explicit consent. This highlights the Shia juristic principle that the trustee’s family holds a legitimate claim to the charity, reflecting the practical wisdom of ensuring the distributor's household is also cared for while fulfilling the charitable obligation.
